Connect to foundations: The virial theorem: why shrinking stars heat up ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01Fast rotation and large angular momentum are different Consider gas in a thin disk on nearly circular orbits around a fixed central mass M. Neglect disk self-gravity and radial pressure corrections and use Newtonian gravity. The model describes radii away from the immediate relativistic vicinity of a black hole. Balance centripetal acceleration against gravity. The orbital speed vφ, angular velocity Ω, and angular momentum per unit mass j then follow: vφ²r = GMr² vφ = √(GMr), Ω = vφr = √(GMr³) j ≡ rvφ = √(GMr) At one-quarter the radius, orbital speed doubles but j halves. Gas accreting through nearly circular orbits must therefore transfer angular momentum elsewhere. Gas that loses energy while retaining j circularizes at rc = j²/(GM). This argument concerns a sequence of circular orbits. An eccentric orbit can change radius during a revolution at fixed angular momentum. Do not generalize the result to every inward motion. 02Outward exchange can release orbital energy Specific orbital energy e is kinetic plus gravitational potential energy. Replacing r by j connects energy directly to angular momentum. e = vφ²2−GMr = −GM2r = −(GM)²2j² dedj = (GM)²j³ = Ω For a ring of fixed mass, the same relation gives dE/dJ = Ω. If an inner ring transfers a small positive δJ to an outer ring, their orbital energy changes are −ΩinδJ and +ΩoutδJ. Since Ωin > Ωout in a Keplerian disk, the total orbital energy decreases. δEorb = (Ωout−Ωin)δJ < 0 δEreleased = (Ωin−Ωout)δJ > 0 The lost orbital energy goes into fluctuations, magnetic fields, heat, radiation, or other channels. The transport mechanism determines where and how much becomes heat. Tracking both angular momentum and energy is the starting point for understanding luminous accretion disks. 03Check conservation with two rings Take equal ring masses m with initial radii r₀ and 4r₀. Use J₀ = m√(GMr₀) and E₀ = GMm/r₀ as angular-momentum and energy units. Transfer δJ = δJ₀ outward and compare circular end states. JinJ₀ = 1−δ, JoutJ₀ = 2+δ rinr₀ = (1−δ)², routr₀ = (2+δ)² The slider controls exchanged angular momentum, not time. Ring masses and central mass remain fixed; the panel compares circular end states. It does not simulate the forces, intermediate trajectories, or disk density evolution. 04Torques and stresses carry angular momentum Torque is the rate of change of angular momentum. Forces between disk regions increase the angular momentum of one and decrease that of the other. Internal exchange does not destroy total angular momentum. 𝒢 = dJdt, [𝒢] = kg m² s−2 Correlated radial and azimuthal velocity fluctuations transport angular momentum through Reynolds stress. Magnetic tension links regions and exchanges angular momentum through Maxwell stress. In sufficiently self-gravitating disks, spiral structure can exert gravitational torques. Transport includes correlations and forces on astrophysical scales, beyond molecular collisional viscosity. The presence of fluctuations alone does not determine the magnitude or direction of transport; the relevant stresses and torques must be identified. 05Build the steady-disk angular-momentum budget Let Σ be surface density and vr radial velocity, positive outward. In a steady disk with no wind or mass sources, the accretion rate dot M, defined positive for inward mass flow, is independent of radius. Ṁ = −2πrΣvr > 0 The outward-positive angular-momentum flux FJ across radius r combines stress transport 𝒢 and inward advection −dot M j. With no accumulation in a steady annulus, FJ is constant with radius. FJ = 𝒢−Ṁj = constant With the boundary condition 𝒢 = 0 at an inner edge rin, the constant is −dot M jin. Rearranging relates inward accretion to the outward stress torque. 𝒢 = Ṁ(j−jin) Zero inner torque is a boundary assumption. Stellar magnetic fields, boundary layers, and stresses near a black hole can change it. A wind removes both mass and angular momentum, so constant dot M and FJ cannot simply be imposed on a wind-driven disk. 06A disk wind provides another route Transferring angular momentum to a wind leaving the disk surfaces can allow the remaining gas to accrete. A magnetically coupled wind can carry rotational angular momentum vertically out of the disk. Distinguish radial exchange within the disk from flux through its surfaces. Ĵwind = Ṁwindjwind Here jwind is angular momentum removed per unit wind mass flux, including the magnetic contribution. A small wind mass flux alone does not imply small angular-momentum removal. Conservation applies to the combined disk and wind, while the disk’s own angular momentum can decrease. Which route dominates a protoplanetary disk depends on its conditions. A magnetized disk wind is distinct from a spherical, thermally driven Parker wind; their driving and angular-momentum budgets need not be the same. 07Connect to alpha, MRI, and disk spreading The alpha model parametrizes transport through an effective kinematic viscosity ν = αcsH, where cs is sound speed and H a vertical scale height. This definition alone does not select the mechanism or determine alpha. ν = αcsH, tν ∼ r²ν H ≈ csΩ ⇒ tν ∼ 1α(rH)²Ω−1 A timescale assuming vertical balance in a thin Keplerian disk and viscous-type radial transport. MRI is a mechanism involving magnetic fields and differential rotation; its requirements differ from self-gravity or winds. Lynden–Bell–Pringle similarity solutions follow accretion and outward spreading with conservation laws and a prescribed ν. Toomre Q introduces gravitational instability. The advanced learning guide connects to alpha disks, MRI, viscous-disk similarity, and Toomre Q. Alpha disks, MRI, and Toomre Q have worked chapters. Viscous-disk similarity develops time evolution from these conservation laws. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. Gas around a fixed central mass moves between nearly circular orbits at r and r/4. How do orbital speed and specific angular momentum change? Does radiating energy alone ensure the required angular-momentum change? Show the answer and reasoning vφ ∝ r−1/2 doubles, while j ∝ r1/2 halves. A torque must transfer angular momentum to other gas or a wind; energy loss alone does not ensure this. The transferred angular momentum remains part of the total budget. Radiation can carry angular momentum in other settings, but that effect is omitted here. REFERENCES & PHYSICAL INPUTS Explanations and derivations are written for this guide. References may use different notation or normalization. Panel methods and approximations are stated in the text.
